title: Fix the Sample Averager
statement:
This one is already written. It compiles without a murmur, it passes the test
the author wrote for it, and it is wrong.

## The bug report

> Averaging filter reports low. Feeding the ADC block eight samples of roughly
> 3000 counts gives an average of about 1500. Shrinking the block to four
> samples makes the fault disappear. Worked fine in the previous release, when
> the sample buffer lived inside the filter module.

The editor starts with the code as it currently stands. Find the defect, fix
it, and leave the rest of the function alone.

## Your function

```
uint16_t average_samples(const uint16_t samples[], size_t count);
```

`samples` points at `count` readings from a 12-bit ADC, so each one is
somewhere in `0 .. 4095`. Return their mean, truncated -- ordinary integer
division, no rounding. `average_samples(x, 0)` is `0`.

## What the tests will tell you

- **four samples, truncated** passes both before and after you fix it. That
  case is in the suite on purpose: it is the shape of data that let this defect
  through review in the first place.
- **eight rising samples** and **sixteen samples across the range** are the
  ones that fail. Read the number that comes back rather than just noting that
  it is wrong -- the size of the error names the culprit.

## Watch out

- The fix is one line, and it is not the loop body, the accumulator type or the
  cast on the way out. Those are all fine.
- `ARRAY_LEN` is a perfectly good macro. It is used in about a thousand real
  embedded projects and it does exactly what it says. That does not mean it
  can answer the question being asked of it here.
- If your first instinct is that the answer would be obvious with a debugger:
  print `n` and see. It is a constant, and it is a constant that has nothing to
  do with this problem's data.

tests.name: eight rising samples
tests.description: The case from the bug report. The true mean is 450; the code as it stands reports the mean of a fixed handful taken from the front of the block.

tests.name: three samples
tests.description: Fewer samples than the broken version tries to read. The elements past the end of the block are zeros in the harness's buffer, which is what drags the answer down.

tests.name: one sample
tests.description: A block of one. The mean of a single reading is that reading.

tests.name: no samples
tests.description: Nothing to average. Return 0 rather than dividing by zero.

tests.name: four samples, truncated
tests.description: 43 / 4 is 10.75, and integer division truncates to 10. This case also passes *before* the fix -- four is the one block length at which the defect is invisible, which is how it survived review.

tests.name: sixteen samples across the range
tests.description: A full-scale ramp in sixteen steps. True mean 2047; a version that averages only the first few reports a few hundred.
